page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The memory configuration consists of 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% of its class. Multi-core performance, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks fall within the average range. However, memory subsystem performance presents a notable tradeoff. While cached, small-block read memory bandwidth is average at 566.42 GB/sec, uncached large-block read bandwidth is weak at 36.85 GB/sec, and large-block write bandwidth is poor, registering in the bottom 10% at 13.83 GB/sec. Text processing performance remains strong, whereas medium-model LLM prompt processing is weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-highcpu-8 offers a dense compute-to-RAM ratio suitable for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores provide predictable execution, though workloads requiring high memory throughput may experience bottlenecks due to the uncached write limitations. This hardware profile is appropriate for web serving, software compilation, text processing, and moderate computational tasks such as lightweight batch processing and single-threaded compression workloads.
